newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent higher.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent a lb higher on Thursday based on market orders at 1017 EDT, traders said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture said 135,000 480-bales of upland cotton were sold, and 94,200 bales were shipped in the week ended July 10.
Traders said the data could buoy prices on the open and pegged resistance at 74.50-75.00 cents in December. Producer selling could limit gains over 75.00 cents, however.
Wednesday, the December contract ended down 0.04 cent 74.20 cents per lb, having ranged from 74.32 to 73.76 cents. The rest of the board finished 0.06 lower to 0.40 cent higher.
An estimated 5,000 lots changed hands on the day.
Support in December remained at 72.00 cents followed by 70.35 cents, the now-expired July contract low.
